note:
Paper 93, Team 46830, the hot-bath optimal-control paper. Fifty-one pages, twenty-four measured
regions over fourteen of them, and the twenty-four resolve into TWELVE FIGURE ROWS, NINE TABLE ROWS
and THREE EXCLUSIONS. Unaccounted zero. Nine of the twelve figures and every one of the nine tables
are printed with a caption; four of the twelve figures and one table are named by a sentence.

Figure 1 is a declared gap rather than a row. Its caption prints at the top of p9 ("Figure 1: The
relationship among the models and equations") with no art anywhere on that page, and the chart itself
starts at the foot of p8, where the extractor boxed only two lettering slices ("Forced convection",
"comfort model") because the diagram's arrows and nodes merge into a single large path. The two
slices are excluded as fragment-of-other; the chart as a whole is recorded here and nowhere else.

Citation is thin. Four of the twelve figure captions are carried into a sentence and eight are named
by nothing: the pointers that do exist are "the fitting plane is shown in Figure 7", "to complete this
action in the form of flow (Fig 8)" - the paper's only abbreviated form - and "As is shown in
Figure 12". Figure 11 is the one exhibit named AFTER it is printed: p33 closes a derivation with
"Where, T (t ) is determined Fig11.", which prints the label as a single word with no space and no
period. Figures 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9 and 10 are named by no sentence, their introductions reading "here
are the results", "the following figure" and nothing at all.

Two placement facts drive the rows. Figure 3's caption prints on the page AFTER its art, so the row
is p12 and the caption is quoted from p13. Figure 10 is a side-by-side pair in one frame with no panel
letters: the left column is lettered "Strategy1" and carries one decision loop, "While sum<1800 (30
minutes)", while the right column is lettered "Strategy2" and carries three, "While Tb< the highest
water temperature", "While Tmin1<Ts" and "While Tmin2<Ts", ending at "Finding the optimal temperature
of adding water/draining". The row order therefore runs right-to-left against the reading order, and
each row keeps its own note.

The tables carry the paper's arithmetic and two of its slips. Table 3 gives the data behind Figure 11
in a grid whose corner cell is split by a diagonal stroke reading "T / t", and its 900 s entry prints
"3143814" with the decimal point missing, so the cell reads as three million instead of about 314.4.
Table 9 prints POSITIVE 0.03% in a column where its sibling Table 5 prints -0.03%, the sign dropped
in a column that is otherwise negative or zero. Otherwise the sensitivity pairs are internally
consistent and the zero column of every grid is 0%: the tub's shape and volume moves water
consumption by up to -85.71% while moving outlet temperature by 0.03%, and the body surface area
moves consumption by -71.43% at +5% while moving temperature by -0.03%, which is the paper's whole
argument in two numbers.

Families: line 3, heatmap-or-contour 2, surface-or-3D 2, flowchart-or-schematic 5, table-grid 9. The
three excluded regions are the two lettering slices of the Figure 1 chart and the second printing of
the Figure 3 clip-art on p44.
rules: Measure first, then read the pixels: twenty-four measured regions resolve into twelve figure rows, nine table rows and three exclusions, and no region is counted twice [place.page_order].

A region boxed as drawn text inside a diagram is a fragment of that diagram, not a figure: two lettering slices of the Figure 1 node-link chart on p8 are excluded as fragment-of-other because the chart's own art is one merged path that the extractor never boxed as a region [place.area_frac].

A printed exhibit with no measured region is a declared gap, not a row: Figure 1's caption prints on p9 with no art on that page and its chart begins at the foot of p8, so the paper's first figure is recorded in this note and in no item [place.doc_order].
The same art printed twice is one exhibit: the p44 raster repeats the p12 clip-art with no caption and no pointer, so p12 is the row and p44 is excluded as a duplicate [place.section_path].

A caption printed on the next page belongs to the art it describes: Figure 3's art sits at the foot of p12 and its caption at the top of p13, so the row is placed on p12 and the caption is quoted from p13 [caption.position].

A side-by-side pair under one caption is one exhibit with two measured boxes: Figure 10's two flow charts are boxed separately, each becomes its own row, each keeps its own note, and both carry the exhibit's panel_count of two [geometry.panel_count].

The reading order of a pair is the printed label, not the box order: Figure 10's left column is lettered 'Strategy1' and its right column 'Strategy2', so the row order and the panel order disagree and the notes say which panel is which [geometry.panel_layout].

Section placement follows the printed heading positions, and where the heading index has dropped the subsection numbering or missed a heading altogether the path quotes the printed line: 5.2.1 to 5.2.3 are indexed as bare list lines and 4.1.3 is not indexed at all, yet all four print on the page [place.section_path].

A pointer that follows its exhibit gives a negative lead: p33 says 'Where, T (t ) is determined Fig11.' about the figure printed on p32, so the first mention page is one past the exhibit page [mention.lead_pages].

caption.verbatim: Table 1 Symbol Table–Constants

mention.lead_sentence: All the variables and constants used in this paper are listed in Table1 and Table 2.

tables.note: The constants table, printed above its own grid on p7: three columns (Symbol, Definition, Value) with one rule under the header and one at the foot, nine rows in all - the header plus eight constants (air temperature at 298K, saturated vapour pressure, water density, specific heat, thermal conductivity, both heat transfer coefficients and the latent heat). No vertical strokes, no shading, units carried inside the Value cells ('298K', '2.26 106 J/kg') rather than in a column of their own. The pointer on the same page spells the label 'Table1' with no space, so the paper never prints 'Table 1' as two words.

caption.verbatim: Table 2 Symbol Table–Variables

mention.lead_sentence: All the variables and constants used in this paper are listed in Table1 and Table 2.

tables.note: The variables table, the taller sibling of Table 1 and the only exhibit in the paper with a Units column: three columns and sixteen rows (header plus fifteen variables - Q, the average temperature, exchange, evaporation, body and radiation heat, T(x,y,z,t), the evaporation rate, flow, outlet temperature, the movement distance and volume of the k-th body position, the forced-convection source, the best flow and the best outlet temperature). Vertical strokes run between the columns so the grid is ruled rather than open, the units sit in the third column as superscripted powers ('m s-1', 'm3 s-1', 'm4'), and the two best-strategy symbols print with a prime (T0', Tb'). The pointer that names both tables is one sentence on p7, a page before this grid.

caption.verbatim: Table 3: Average temperature data

tables.note: The numbers behind Figure 11, printed directly under it: seven columns (a corner cell reading 'T / t' split by a diagonal stroke, then six time points 300, 600, 900, 1200, 1500 and 1800 s) and three rows in all - the time header, the average temperature row and the second row the caption does not explain. One vertical stroke separates the corner label from the data, the rest of the grid is open. DATA DEFECT: the 900 s entry prints '3143814' with no decimal point where its neighbours give 316.0650, 315.1926, 313.6271, so the cell reads as three million instead of about 314.4 - the one arithmetic error a reader can catch by eye in the whole paper.
